narrative:
The model estimates an 80% chance that you will leave your job. In practical terms, among employees with a profile like yours, the model expects about 8 in 10 to depart, so your promotion was denied because the organization sees a high retention risk rather than a strong likelihood that you will remain and grow in the role.

The strongest reason was that you reported having other job opportunities. That was the most influential signal and pushed the prediction toward leaving; only about 23% of employees predicted to stay said they had other opportunities. Your total years of experience also pushed toward leaving and ranked second. You have 6–10 years of overall experience, whereas about half of employees predicted to stay have only 1–5 years. Third, working in the “other” sector added further pressure toward leaving; that sector accounts for about 22% of employees predicted to stay. All three top signals pointed in the same direction, toward departure.

Before revisiting promotion, you and your manager should discuss your career path, how your other opportunities compare with internal prospects, and what would make you want to stay. The organization should also examine whether your experience and sector context are creating a retention gap that a clearer development plan or promotion pathway could address.
